title: Ordinary nonnegativity and constant degree zero of normalized potentials
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and $X$ a Noetherian excellent normal integral scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $\eta$ be its generic point [def-weil-residue-field], and let $\delta$ be a dimension function with $\delta(\eta)=0$. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ be a pinned potential dualizing complex for $(X,\delta,\Lambda)$ [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Then $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<0$, and the generic pinning extends uniquely to an isomorphism $\mathcal H^0(K)\cong\Lambda_X$. Equivalently it gives a canonical isomorphism $\Lambda_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\mathrm{ord}}_{\leq0}K$, hence a canonical map $\Lambda_X\to K$. These maps commute with restriction to etale schemes and localizations, and with pinning-preserving morphisms of $K$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 3.6.4 and its proof (printed p. 279)

proof.text: Prepare the strict-local reduction. For a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, choose a normal affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and put $S=X_{(\bar x)}=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{X,x}^{sh})$. Localization preserves Noetherianity and excellence. The strict-henselization triples give a local filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras, hence a normal domain with injective map from $A$. Its Noetherianity follows from that of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. It is excellent because an ind-etale map is weakly etale and a Noetherian weakly etale algebra over an excellent ring is excellent. Thus $S$ is again Noetherian excellent normal integral, its generic point maps to $\eta$, and $\ell$ remains invertible. All these arguments also apply to strict localizations of $S$ and of its open subschemes.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.4, first reduction; 2.2.1 and following paragraph (strict localization).

proof.text: Record the local data the induction uses, without asserting that a restriction of $K$ carries pinnings on residue-field sites. For a geometric point $\bar x$ over $x\in X$ put $S=X_{(\bar x)}$, $u:S\to X$ and $K_S=u^*K$, which lies in $D^+(S_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ because inverse image is exact and preserves the constant ring. (i) Generic pinning: the generic point $\eta_S$ lies over $\eta$ (step 1), and pulling $p_\eta$ back along $\eta_S\to\eta$ gives $p_{\eta_S}:K_S|_{\eta_S}\simeq\Lambda_{\eta_S}$. (ii) Closed costalk: the closed point $s$ has separably closed residue field, so sheaves on $s_{\mathrm{et}}$ are $\Lambda$-modules and $R\Gamma_sK_S=i_s^!K_S$; the prime-power costalk reduction identifies it with the geometric fibre $C_{\bar x}(K)$, and the geometric fibre of $p_x$ gives $q_{\bar x}:i_s^!K_S\simeq\Lambda(\delta(x))[2\delta(x)]$. (iii) Transitivity: $u$ is ind-etale, being on an affine chart the filtered colimit of etale algebras of the triples, and so is an open immersion of $S$ or a localization (a colimit of principal opens). For a geometric point $\bar z$ of $S$, or of an open $U\subset S$, strict-local invariance gives an $X$-isomorphism $U_{(\bar z)}\simeq S_{(\bar z)}\simeq X_{(u\bar z)}$; under it the restriction of $K_S$ is that of $K$, and by functoriality of inverse image along $\eta_{X_{(u\bar z)}}\to\eta_S\to\eta$ the pulled-back generic pinnings agree. The transition equalities of the definition and pinnings at non-closed points of $S$ are not used below.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 2.2.1 and its following paragraph; Definitions 1.4.1 and 2.1.2.

proof.text: Fix the canonical comparison before proving it is invertible. Write $a:\eta\to X$ and let $p_\eta:a^*K\simeq\Lambda_\eta$ be the generic pinning. Exact inverse image and its compatibility with cohomology give $a^*\mathcal H^0K\simeq\Lambda_\eta$. By the sheaf adjunction define $b_X:\mathcal H^0K\to a_*\Lambda_\eta$ to be the map adjoint to this isomorphism, and set $\beta_X=c_a^{-1}b_X:\mathcal H^0K\to\Lambda_X$, where $c_a:\Lambda_X\simeq a_*\Lambda_\eta$ is the normal-constant-generic isomorphism. This construction does not assume nonnegativity. It commutes with restriction to a normal integral localization or strict localization: the comparison $u^*a_*\Lambda_\eta\to a'_*\Lambda_{\eta'}$ sends the pullback of the constant section $\lambda$ to the same section $\lambda$, so under $c_a,c_{a'}$ it is the identity of $\Lambda_Y$; adjunction then identifies $u^*\beta_X$ with $\beta_Y$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 3.6.4, generic pinning and final sentence; Stacks 09Z5, lemma-push-constant-sheaf-from-open.

proof.text: Compute $\delta$ on $X$ and set up the induction. For $x\in X$ the Noetherian local domain $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ has finite dimension $r$; choose a chain $0=\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_r=\mathfrak m_x$ of maximal length, with points $y_0=\eta,\dots,y_r=x$. Each link is saturated, so the closure $Z_k$ of $y_k$ has $\dim\mathcal O_{Z_k,y_{k+1}}=1$. As $\mathcal O_{X,y_{k+1}}\to\mathcal O^{sh}_{X,y_{k+1}}$ is faithfully flat, some point of $X_{(\bar y_{k+1})}$ lies over $y_k$; by part (a) of the criterion its closure has dimension one, so a geometric point over it gives an immediate geometric specialization. Thus $\delta(y_k)=\delta(y_{k+1})+1$, and telescoping from $\delta(\eta)=0$ gives $\delta(x)=-\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Let $P(d)$ say: for every geometric point $\bar x$ over $x$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=d$, with $S=X_{(\bar x)}$ as in step 2, $\mathcal H^q(K_S)=0$ for $q<0$ and $\beta_S$ is an isomorphism. We prove $P(d)$ by strong induction on $d$; finiteness of local dimensions makes this cover every point. Here $\dim S=d$ by strict-henselization dimension. If $z\in S$ is not the closed point $s$, any chain ending at $\mathfrak p_z$ extends by $\mathfrak p_z\subsetneq\mathfrak m_s$, so $\dim\mathcal O_{S,z}<d$, and by step 2(iii) and strict-henselization dimension $\dim\mathcal O_{X,u(z)}=\dim\mathcal O^{sh}_{X,u(z)}=\dim\mathcal O^{sh}_{S,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{S,z}<d$.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.4: induction on d; XIV, Proposition 2.1.4 for immediate specializations.

proof.text: For $d=0$, the local domain is a field and its generic point is all of $S$. The generic pinning is then $K_S\simeq\Lambda_S$ in degree zero, proving both the vanishing and invertibility of $\beta_S$. For $d\geq1$, let $j:U=S-\{s\}\hookrightarrow S$. The open $U$ is Noetherian; excellence, normality and integrality hold by restriction. At each $z\in U$, step 2(iii) identifies $U_{(\bar z)}$ with $X_{(u\bar z)}$, compatibly with $K$ and the generic pinnings, and step 4 gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X,u(z)}<d$, so the induction hypothesis $P(\dim\mathcal O_{X,u(z)})$ applies there. Exact inverse image commutes with cohomology, and step 3 identifies the restriction of $\beta_U$ with that comparison. The conservative geometric stalks now give $\mathcal H^q(K_S|_U)=0$ for $q<0$ and the canonical isomorphism $\beta_U:\mathcal H^0(K_S|_U)\simeq\Lambda_U$. Thus the induction is applied only at smaller strict-local dimensions, not to the possibly nonlocal open $U$ as though it were local.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.4: base case and hypothesis on U.

proof.text:
Let $i:s\hookrightarrow S$. By step 4, $\delta(x)=-d$, so step 2(ii) gives $i^!K_S\simeq\Lambda(-d)[-2d]$, which has cohomology only in degree $2d\geq2$. Closed direct image is exact (the support-kernel adjunction), so $\mathcal H^q(i_*i^!K_S)=0$ for $q\leq1$. The supported-kernel adjunction and the bounded-below derived adjunction identify this $i^!$ with the right adjoint used in the closed-support triangle. Indeed, represent $K_S$ by a bounded-below injective complex $I$, which is K-injective; $i^!_0$ is right adjoint to the exact $i_*$, so it preserves injectives, and both derived Hom groups out of $i_*G$ are the homotopy classes $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*G,I)=\operatorname{Hom}(G,i^!_0I)$, with the same counit. Consequently that triangle is
$$i_*i^!K_S\longrightarrow K_S\longrightarrow Rj_*(K_S|_U)\longrightarrow i_*i^!K_S[1].$$
The support adjunction is $\Lambda$-linear: the kernel and inverse-image constructions preserve the scalar action, so its abelian-sheaf bijection restricts to the bijection on $\Lambda$-linear maps. Exactness of closed direct image on module sheaves follows by the exact faithful forgetful functor.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.4: localization triangle and pinning at the closed point.

proof.text:
Compute the two lowest ranges of the last term. Put $L=K_S|_U$. Since $L$ is nonnegative, choose an injective representative $I$ zero in degrees below zero. It computes $Rj_*L$ by termwise $j_*$. Thus $Rj_*L$ has no negative cohomology, and left exactness gives
$$\mathcal H^0(Rj_*L)=\ker(j_*I^0\to j_*I^1)=j_*\ker(I^0\to I^1)=j_*\mathcal H^0L.$$
This identification respects the adjunction map, since it is induced by kernels of the termwise map. There is no appeal to exactness of $j_*$ in positive degrees.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.4: inference from the triangle; Stacks derived.tex 05TI/05TH and the kernel calculation.

proof.text:
Apply the cohomology long exact sequence to step 6. For $q<0$, both adjacent cohomology objects of $i_*i^!K_S$ vanish and the middle comparison identifies $\mathcal H^qK_S$ with the zero object $\mathcal H^qRj_*L$. For $q=0$, the same reasoning uses precisely degrees $0$ and $1$ of the supported term, yielding
$$\mathcal H^0K_S\xrightarrow{\sim}j_*\mathcal H^0L\xrightarrow{j_*\beta_U}\ j_*\Lambda_U.$$
The open $U$ is nonempty, as $d\geq1$ and it contains the generic point. Normality and integrality of $S$ therefore give $c_j:\Lambda_S\xrightarrow{\sim}j_*\Lambda_U$. Composing with $c_j^{-1}$ gives an isomorphism $\mathcal H^0K_S\simeq\Lambda_S$. Its generic restriction is $p_{\eta_S}$, since all comparison maps came from the adjunction unit and $\beta_U$. By adjunction into $a_*\Lambda_{\eta_S}\simeq\Lambda_S$, a map to this target is uniquely determined by its generic restriction. Thus this isomorphism is exactly $\beta_S$ of step 3, completing the induction.

source.place: XVII, last three sentences of the proof of Lemma 3.6.4; Stacks 09Z5 for the open and generic units.

proof.text: Return to arbitrary $X$. By step 4, $P(d)$ holds for every $d$, so it applies to every $X_{(\bar x)}$. Steps 2 and 3 identify its negative cohomology and canonical comparison with the inverse images of those of $K$. Exactness of geometric stalks and commutation of exact functors with cohomology show that all negative cohomology stalks vanish and that every stalk of $\beta_X$ is invertible. Conservative geometric stalks give $\mathcal H^qK=0$ for $q<0$ and $\beta_X:\mathcal H^0K\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X$. No global finite-dimensional bound on $X$ has been used.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.4, first sentence and strict-local induction.

proof.text: The extension is unique: any map $\mathcal H^0K\to\Lambda_X$ extending $p_\eta$ becomes, after $c_a$, a map to $a_*\Lambda_\eta$ with fixed adjoint, and so equals $b_X$. A pinning-preserving $v:K\to K'$ satisfies $p'_\eta a^*v=p_\eta$; hence $\beta_{K'}\mathcal H^0(v)=\beta_K$ by the same adjunction. For etale restriction, work locally on each normal integral component supplied by the normal-component lemma. A nonempty etale component has open image, since an etale morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation, so its generic point lies above $\eta$; its generic pinning is the pullback of $p_\eta$. As in step 3 the comparison of the two generic direct images sends $\lambda$ to $\lambda$, so the pulled-back isomorphism extends that pinning and uniqueness identifies it with $\beta_{u^*K}$. This also proves compatibility for localizations and strict localizations by step 3. The empty etale scheme has a unique comparison. Since these assertions are local on the etale source, no quasi-compactness of that source is needed.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 3.6.4 and Proposition 2.2.1: uniqueness and restriction functoriality of the generic extension.

proof.text:
Finally use ordinary smart truncation. In a representing cochain complex, $\tau_{\leq0}K$ has the terms below degree zero unchanged and cycles in degree zero. Its canonical projection onto the single complex $\mathcal H^0K[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism because all negative cohomology vanishes. Inverting that projection and composing with $\beta_X^{-1}$ gives
$$\Lambda_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\mathrm{ord}}_{\leq0}K\longrightarrow K.$$
Exact inverse image preserves kernels, images and their quotients, so termwise pullback commutes with this smart truncation, its projection onto $\mathcal H^0$, and its inclusion into $K$. These maps are also natural in complex maps; on the derived category the same equalities hold by localization. The uniqueness and functorialities established in step 10 therefore give all asserted compatibilities of the truncation isomorphism and of the map to $K$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 3.6.4, statement after Autrement dit; explicit ordinary truncation construction.
